---
title: Available card catalogue
---

`app/data/card_catalogue.json` is a versioned metadata cache keyed by card module ID. Records contain module, long_name, plain-text description, mutable, pipeline_compatible and a SHA-256 source fingerprint. Native startup reads it through `Module.card_catalogue`. Metadata describes the declared card behaviour, not successful runtime validation for every dataset.

Discovery continues to use `app/cards/*.py`, excluding `__init__`, `sys_bookmark` and `template` as before. Missing, corrupt, unknown-version or source-stale records fall back to filenames. Missing descriptive properties also fall back gracefully. Discovery and opening the picker never instantiate all cards. Removed files cease to be offered even if an old cache record remains.

Lazy capture happens after a normal factory returns in `app.py:create_card`, and before `Card.call_ui()` for standalone use. Constructors in Module/Card are too early because factories subsequently assign metadata. `Module.update_card_catalogue()` records completed values. Unchanged entries do not cause disk writes. Entries are shared per process, writes merge newer on-disk records, use a native POSIX interprocess lock, and replace JSON atomically under an in-process lock. The lock file is ignored by Git. On native platforms without POSIX locking, atomic replacement and in-process locking remain available.

`PYTHAGORAS_CARD_CATALOGUE_PATH` optionally selects another writable native JSON path. The default is the bundled catalogue, allowing development use to update it as cards are created. An absent or unwritable cache does not prevent card use: updated metadata remains in memory and a warning is logged. Do not store session namespaces, user data or bookmark decisions in this file.

The Manage cards and sections modal is extra-wide. Its searchable selectize control matches long name, module ID and description, while the selected-card panel displays the description and mutability/compatibility flags. Option values remain unchanged module IDs. Filenames remain valid selections when metadata is unavailable. Adding a card and managing sections retain their existing validation.

Rebuild card catalogue launches a cancellable background task with a separate Python subprocess. The worker imports each discovered module and calls its factory without mounting UI or starting servers. It captures final metadata and clears only its own Module.Instances registry after each card. It never constructs catalogue-probe cards inside the live app. Failed imports/factories are reported individually and preserve existing valid records or filename fallbacks. A worker failure or 180-second timeout leaves the previous catalogue usable. Cancellation/session closure terminates the worker. Results merge into the parent cache; files changed during the rebuild are not accepted as current metadata. Rebuilding preserves the picker selection and live card sequence.

Shinylive reads the bundled catalogue and updates metadata in memory during ordinary use. It does not try to persist to the deployed filesystem or launch subprocesses; its rebuild button is unavailable with an explanation. To refresh its bundled descriptions, rebuild in a native checkout before exporting the app.

Native maintenance can also generate a worker result without opening the app:

```sh
.venv/bin/python app/card_catalogue.py --worker --output /tmp/card-catalogue-result.json
```

The worker result includes per-card errors. The modal merges successful records into the maintained catalogue. The shipped seed was generated by isolated eager discovery of all currently available cards.
